theorem_I.statement: M2 and M3a both land in orb(sigma^L u) (the nu-target orbit); M3b and M3c land in a THIRD orbit (neither own nor nu-target)
theorem_I.consequence: for a FULL pass the nu-target orbit IS its own orbit, so M3a is an intra-run x-arc and is FORBIDDEN when x = 0; hence every paid exit of a full pass is M3b or M3c, i.e. a Round-115 light connector

theorem_II.statement: M2 lands at phase(entry(nu(p))) + 1 and M3a at + 2, for every word and every pass length

m3a_contraction.corollary_IV: a paid ascent exit fails to create a contractible block ONLY when it is M3b or M3c - because M3a lands in the nu-target orbit at +2 and still reaches nu(p). This is a sharper characterisation of 'M-off-target' than 'the paid exit targets the wrong orbit'
m3a_contraction.reproves: Round-135's u parameter: u = number of M3a-type contractions

capacity_growth.law: N*(b,0,s) = N*(0,0,s) + 15b   (+3 orbits, +4 runs per token)
capacity_growth.status: verified on every exhaustively computed cell available; stated as an EMPIRICAL law, not proved in general
capacity_growth.orbit_reach: at s = 13 a pure light chain reaches 19 + 3b orbits
capacity_growth.consequence: the (3,2) target object has 27 orbits, so as a PURE light chain it would need 19 + 3b >= 27, i.e. b >= 3. Since b = e here, every row with e <= 2 CANNOT be a pure light chain - its short-pass connectors are structurally indispensable

derivation: #ascents = F = 2, so #(free ascents) = 2 - a with a = #(nonfree ascents)
each free descent opens a distinct repeat run, so d := #(free descents) <= e; put eta := e - d >= 0
delta = F + e - f_out = 2 + e - (2 - a) - d = a + (e - d) = a + eta
delta_decomposition.dichotomy: delta = 1 forces (a, eta) = (1,0) [mechanism M] or (0,1) [mechanism R]
delta_decomposition.M_needs: e = d <= #descents, so e <= 1 (type A) and e <= 2 (type B)
delta_decomposition.R_needs: d = e - 1 <= #descents, so e <= 2 (type A) and e <= 3 (type B)

n4_adversarial.verdict: Theorems I-III are not n=6-specific: they hold verbatim at n=4, so they carry no hidden n=6 hypothesis
